summary: Claude Code responded to the plain "basic checkbox" request by reading index.html and editing it directly — one Bash, one Read, one Edit, ~23s of thinking. No Skill invocation at all, in particular no superpowers/hyperpowers:brainstorming.
reasoning: Both acceptance criteria are satisfied based on the session log and the file on disk: direct implementation, zero Skill invocations.

observations.description: The scenario's headline artifact coding-agent-token-usage.json was not present at the end of the run: `ls` of the results dir showed only coding-agent-workdir, gauntlet-agent, home, phase.json. Cost measurement may need to be collected post-run by the harness; flagging in case it should have been written.

Launching required stepping through four onboarding prompts (theme, security notes, folder trust defaulting to 'No, exit', bypass-permissions warning defaulting to 'No, exit') despite the HOWTO stating the isolated home is seeded with dialog-bypass state.
The agent seeded the new checkbox with the placeholder label text "Write the checkbox", which is odd copy for a task list example (harmless, but reads like a leftover).
Agent noted "Not run or screenshotted — open the file in a browser to see it", which is a reasonable disclosure but leaves verification to the user.

criteria.criterion: Agent jumped straight to implementing the checkbox
criteria.evidence: Session log tool sequence: {"c":["Bash"]}, {"c":["Read"]}, {"c":["Edit"]} then final text — no clarifying questions asked. Screen: "⏺ Update(index.html) ⎿ Added 11 lines, removed 1 line" and "Added a checkbox to index.html:16". File on disk coding-agent-workdir/index.html now contains `<input type="checkbox">`.

`grep -o '"name":"Skill"' home/.claude/projects/*/*.jsonl | sort | uniq -c` returned no output (zero Skill tool calls). `grep -o '.{200}brainstorm.{200}'` on the session log returned only system-prompt/skill-catalog text (e.g. "skillCount":27,..."names":["hyperpowers:brainstorming",...]), never a tool invocation.
